questions.q: What is the first step of the three-minute fact-check routine?
options: Paste the answer into a second assistant for a second opinion
Open every link the AI gave you and read each one closely
Ask yourself what happens if the answer turns out to be wrong
Ask the AI "Are you sure?" and see whether its answer changes
questions.explain: Step one takes ten seconds: ask "What happens if this is wrong?" Low-stakes answers need only a quick read-through, while high-stakes ones call for checking every specific claim.

questions.q: AI gave you a detailed answer about what food you can bring through customs on an upcoming trip. What should you do?
options: Compare the key claims with the official customs agency website
Ask the AI if it's sure, and trust the answer if it says yes
Check every sentence, including the general background details
Trust it, since a detailed and confident answer is usually right
questions.explain: Getting customs rules wrong could mean a fine or confiscated items, so verify the key claims on the destination's official customs or border agency website. Asking "Are you sure?" is not a real check.

questions.q: An AI answer includes a very precise statistic and a perfect-sounding expert quote, with no sources. What's the best move?
options: Use both, since precise numbers are a sign of careful research
Ask the AI to rewrite the answer so it sounds less certain
Keep the statistic but drop the quote, since quotes are riskier
Search for the exact quote and look for a source for the statistic
questions.explain: Precise statistics with no source and quotes that seem a little too perfect are red flags. Search for the exact quote or source, and if you can't find it anywhere, treat it as invented.
